summary: Do not ship this walking skeleton yet: the central single-Writer-Lane invariant is not enforced by its public interface, and later Backup increments would spread that unsound contract.
triage: review-gate SKILL.md rules govern: render EVERY finding as a full table row, the human decides each row (accept/reject/defer/question — free text), echo back before applying, max 2 rounds, append decisions.md and COMMIT it with this artifact.

findings.title: `Held` is an escapable, independently mintable token—not proof of active ownership
findings.body: `run<T>` can return its `Held` value, so `const held = await createWriterLane().run(async h => h); await persistState(held, state)` type-checks while writing outside the lane. The public factory also creates unlimited independent tails. `persistState` merely accepts and ignores the token (`src/platform/stateStore.ts:87-95`). The renderer guard does not close this: its regex only follows static imports and hard-codes two entrypoints (`src/runtime/renderer-boundary.test.ts:28-72`), while this repository already uses renderer-side `import()`. A renderer or later timer refactor can therefore obtain/reuse a valid token, establish another lane, and restore the lost-update corruption while typecheck and the structural test remain green. Tickets 02–03 would propagate this signature to every Backup mutation, making correction substantially costlier.
findings.recommendation: Replace the bearer-token seam before extending it: keep raw storage writers private to a worker-owned mutation service and expose methods that always enqueue on its single lane, with a private scoped interface only for nested reset work. At minimum, make lane creation worker-private, validate lane identity and active lifetime at runtime, and replace the regex guard with an AST/bundler graph covering dynamic imports and all renderer entrypoints.

next_steps: Redesign the Writer Lane capability boundary, then rerun the structure gate before beginning tickets 02–03.
